localChanges: A game now ends when you conquer the world, when the final year arrives (2100 on Chieftain, down to 2020 on Emperor), or when you choose Game → Retire. You see why it ended, your Civilization Score and your Civilization Rating against history's famous leaders, and you can keep playing afterwards with no further score (closes #176).
You are warned 20 years before the final year that your leader plans to retire.
If your civilization is destroyed, the archaeologists tell its story instead of the game quietly restarting. You are only out of the game once you have no cities and no Settlers left.
The Game menu now has Retire and Quit, and Quit takes you back to the main menu (closes #362).

A spaceship that reaches Alpha Centauri always lands, and the first to land wins the game. Losing your capital sends your spaceship back to Earth, or cancels it if it hasn't launched, and the same happens to any civilization that is destroyed (closes #177).
When a civilization completes the Apollo Program, every civilization can now build a spaceship. Civilizations that had already moved that turn used to miss out.
Your best games are kept in a Hall of Fame, shown when a game ends and from the main menu (closes #179).
